claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys have strong mechanical properties at elevated temperatures.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy that can exist in a high-temperature BCC phase.
A silicide coating can be applied to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by pack cementation.
Silicide coating improves the oxidation resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Adding an appropriate amount of silicon to refractory high-entropy alloys can promote a dense surface film and improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Applying a silicide-based coating to the RHEA will form a dense, stable silicide layer.
The silicide layer will act as a diffusion barrier in molten aluminum.
The silicide layer will limit direct contact and chemical interaction between molten aluminum and the refractory-alloy substrate.
Limiting aluminum–substrate interaction will reduce corrosion and erosion of the RHEA.
Silicide-coated RHEA components will resist molten-aluminum erosion significantly better than uncoated RHEA components.
Silicide-coated RHEA components will have lower weight loss and less surface degradation after prolonged molten-aluminum exposure than uncoated RHEAs.
Silicide-coated RHEA components will have lower weight loss and less surface degradation than conventional materials such as untreated steels.
Coating degradation or delamination during very long exposure or severe thermal cycling may diminish the protective effect.
Coating uniformity and integrity are critical to protection against molten aluminum.
The long-term stability and magnitude of the silicide coating's benefit in direct molten-aluminum exposure remain unquantified.
